detail:
The MedlinePlus encyclopedia describes generalized anxiety disorder as a mental disorder in which a person is often worried or anxious about many things and finds it hard to control the anxiety. The encyclopedia notes there is no test that makes the diagnosis, which is based on the person's answers to questions about symptoms, and that the main symptom is frequent worry or tension for at least 6 months, even when there is little or no clear cause.

For treatment, the encyclopedia describes the goal as helping the person feel better and function well in daily life, with talk therapy, medicine, or a combination described as the approaches clinicians use. Psychotherapy described in the sources includes cognitive-behavioral therapy, and medicine classes described include antidepressant medicines, which the encyclopedia notes can take time to start working and are also used for anxiety. Follow-up in the sources tracks symptoms and functioning over time, and treatment plans are described as made together by the person and the clinician.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about managing generalized anxiety disorder and medicines.
summary: The MedlinePlus encyclopedia describes generalized anxiety disorder management with talk therapy, medicine, or both, including cognitive-behavioral therapy and antidepressant medicine classes, with treatment plans made by the person and clinician together.
takeaways: no single test makes the diagnosis, the encyclopedia describes
talk therapy, medicine, or both are the approaches sources describe
never start, stop, or change medicines without your doctor
title: Managing generalized anxiety disorder day to day
